evidence.legacySpeculative: Legacy estimate from stream chunks; this is not engine-reported speculative decoding evidence.
evidence.noEligible: No measured point has sufficient evidence and meets the configured constraints.
evidence.title: Request and session evidence
evidence.missing: This point has no supported session or round evidence. Historical identities and cache states cannot be reconstructed.
evidence.percentiles: P50 / P99 with valid sample count n. Last output and stream completion are measured separately.
evidence.ignoreEOSRequested: Fixed length requested; verify observed output
evidence.contextPeak: Peak input + output of one request
evidence.localEstimate: Token distributions cover successful requests. Local counts are estimates without the service chat template; they are retained separately from server usage.
evidence.cacheIndependent: Round number does not prove a cache hit. Design reuse, server cache usage and observed latency are separate evidence.
evidence.sessionTruncated: Only a bounded set of session records is shown; aggregate counts include every session.
evidence.timelineExport: The HTML export includes retained request timelines and links to individual requests. Request detail may be disabled, unavailable or truncated.

benchmarkError.BENCHMARK_SERVER_RESTARTED: The server restarted and interrupted the evaluation; completed points were retained.

benchmarkWarning.BENCHMARK_TOKENIZER_LOAD_FAILED: The requested tokenizer could not be loaded. New evaluations stop before inference; older runs may have used estimated lengths. Check the run status and evidence.
benchmarkWarning.BENCHMARK_AGENTIC_LENGTH_DRIFT: Measured mean input differs from the Agentic design target by more than 10%; check the tokenizer and server chat template.
benchmarkWarning.BENCHMARK_CONFLICT_OVERRIDDEN: This evaluation was started on top of an already running one; both share GPUs and node resources, so their results may be depressed.
benchmarkWarning.BENCHMARK_WARMUP_UNSUPPORTED: The load-origin agent predates warmup, so no warmup requests were sent; the first point may include cold-start overhead.

wizard.tokenizerControlledHelp: Token-length workloads require a loadable tokenizer. Missing or failed tokenizers stop evaluation before any inference request. Locally generated lengths can still differ from endpoint usage because of chat templates and tokenization.
wizard.tokenizerHelp: Natural dataset text can run without a tokenizer; local counts are estimates, separate from endpoint-reported usage.
wizard.tokenizerManagedHelp: Managed models can usually resolve their tokenizer automatically. Token-length workloads stop if it is unavailable; natural dataset text can use estimated local counts.
wizard.tokenizerAgenticHelp: Agentic turn lengths and designed prefix reuse are token-based. Estimation error accumulates across turns and can exceed the context limit, so a tokenizer is required.
wizard.tokenizerAutoHelp: Uses the tokenizer.json already on the target machine; when the load origin is the server it is fetched back over the data lane, and the model repository is the fallback when there is none.

wizard.legacySLADropped: The source run's per-user throughput limits used the retired throughput ÷ concurrency definition and were not carried over; use the Interactivity floor instead.
wizard.requestRatesHelp: Each rate is one point: requests arrive at that rate without waiting for earlier ones; combined with every ISL/OSL.
wizard.requestRatesInvalid: Enter 1–{{count}} numbers greater than 0 and at most {{max}}
wizard.pointDurationHelp: How long each point keeps sending requests; requests = rate × duration, at least {{min}}.
wizard.loadModeHelp: Fixed concurrency (closed loop) keeps N requests in flight and sends the next only when one returns. Arrival rate (open loop) sends requests on a Poisson/gamma schedule regardless of earlier ones, which is closer to production traffic and exposes queueing tail latency.
wizard.burstinessHelp: Gamma shape of the gaps between arrivals: 1 is Poisson, below 1 burstier, above 1 more even.
wizard.maxInFlightHelp: Cap on requests in flight, 0 for none; arrivals over the cap queue on the client and are timed from when they are actually sent.
wizard.warmupRequestsHelp: Requests sent before the first point and discarded, to keep first-request cold start (CUDA graphs, compilation, caches) out of the results. 0 disables warmup.
wizard.ignoreEOSHelp: Asks the engine to ignore the end-of-sequence token and generate the full target output length, so throughput compares across models and engines. Some SaaS endpoints reject the parameter with 400; turn it off for them.

metricHelp.pareto: One dot per point: Interactivity (1000 / TPOT P50) across, output throughput up. Up and to the right is better: right is faster per user, up is more total output.
metricHelp.output: All output tokens of the point ÷ the point's wall time, from the first request sent to the last one finished: the system's total output rate.
metricHelp.total: Input + output tokens ÷ the point's wall time.
metricHelp.request: Successful requests ÷ the point's wall time.
metricHelp.interactivity: Tokens per second one request receives once decoding has started = 1000 / TPOT P50, excluding TTFT (InferenceMAX interactivity).
metricHelp.ttft: Time to first token: from sending the request to its first token, including queueing and prefill.
metricHelp.tpot: Time per output token: (E2E latency − TTFT) ÷ (output tokens − 1), per request.
metricHelp.latency: End-to-end latency: from sending the request to its last token.
metricHelp.maxOutput: Highest output throughput over any 10-second window of the point, free of ramp-up and drain dilution.
metricHelp.maxTotal: Highest total throughput over any 10-second window of the point.
metricHelp.requestRate: Mean arrival rate of requests under arrival-rate load.
metricHelp.concurrency: Requests kept in flight under fixed concurrency; the in-flight cap under arrival-rate load.
